rows.opening: That weight lifting must be real—what was the actual sticking point?

Two-hundred change hits differently when it comes from someone who already has their foot under you—it stops being abstract numbers and starts feeling like a squeeze, especially if work or other costs have tightened up since last year.
The gap after snapping sounds heavier than a simple misunderstanding—like it opened up more distance in your world somehow, not just with her but maybe somewhere inside yourself too.
That kind of move says something about how much you mean to her—she just *knew* what mattered most and acted on it before you had a chance to ask for help yourself.
That stillness sounds like it came from somewhere you needed—not something that happened to you alone but space your body finally got back in.

That jump from sleep deprivation directly into that buzz makes sense—your nervous system was already on edge before you even sat down for work this week; what made it worse about stands-up specifically?
That's exactly what happens when you prep something properly—the room shifts, people notice it too.
That gap between when you read something—like the time it arrived vs.
The numbness of it—talking past each other yet your body refusing silence with him over something so small like a phone call feels telling.
